## Solution

**Define the linear change of variables:**

Let
$$u = 3x - 2y + z, \quad v = 2x + 3y - z, \quad w = x - 3y + z.$$

Then the vector field becomes $F = (u,\, v,\, w)$, and the surface $S$ becomes the octahedron
$$|u| + |v| + |w| = 1.$$

**Divergence of $F$:**

$$\nabla \cdot F = \frac{\partial}{\partial x}(3x-2y+z) + \frac{\partial}{\partial y}(2x+3y-z) + \frac{\partial}{\partial z}(x-3y+z) = 3 + 3 + 1 = 7.$$

**Jacobian of the transformation:**

$$J = \frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \end{pmatrix}.$$

$$\det J = 3(3\cdot1 - (-1)(-3)) -(-2)(2\cdot1-(-1)\cdot1) + 1(2\cdot(-3)-3\cdot1)$$
$$= 3(3-3) + 2(2+1) + (-6-3) = 0 + 6 - 9 = -3.$$

So $|\det J| = 3$, and $dV_{uvw} = 3\, dV_{xyz}$, i.e. $dV_{xyz} = \tfrac{1}{3}\,dV_{uvw}$.

**Volume of the octahedron in $(u,v,w)$-space:**

The region $|u|+|v|+|w|\le 1$ is a regular octahedron. By symmetry, in the first octant ($u,v,w\ge 0$, $u+v+w\le 1$) it is a tetrahedron with volume $\frac{1}{6}$. Across all 8 octants:

$$\text{Vol}_{uvw} = 8 \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{4}{3}.$$

**Volume in $(x,y,z)$-space:**

$$\text{Vol}_{xyz} = \frac{\text{Vol}_{uvw}}{|\det J|} = \frac{4/3}{3} = \frac{4}{9}.$$

**Apply the Divergence Theorem:**

$$\iint_S F \cdot n\, dS = \iiint_V (\nabla \cdot F)\, dV = 7 \cdot \frac{4}{9} = \frac{28}{9}.$$

The flux of $F$ through $S$ is $\boxed{\dfrac{28}{9}}$.
